about: A garden on the school roof

lines.text: Few visitors to our school ever guess what lies above the science laboratories.
Three years ago, the flat roof were nothing more than bare grey concrete,
lines.note: Agreement: 'the flat roof' is one thing, so it is 'was'.

lines.text: but a group of teachers decided to turn it into an garden. They
lines.note: Article: 'garden' starts with a consonant sound, so it is 'a garden'.

lines.text: began with a few pots of chilli and basil. Today, more than forty
kinds of vegetables and herbs are grew there in long wooden boxes. Every
lines.note: Verb form: after 'are' it is 'grown', not 'grew'.

lines.text: morning, members of the Gardening Club water the plants careful before lessons begin.
lines.note: Word form: 'water' is a verb here, so it takes the adverb 'carefully'.

lines.text: They also check the leaves for snails, who can ruin a whole
crop overnight. The work is tiring, so nobody complains because the results are
lines.note: Connector: the two ideas contrast, so it is 'but', not 'so'.

lines.text: easy to see. Once a month, the harvest is sold to parents and
teachers at a small stall. Several student have even started growing vegetables at
home. Our principal says the garden has taught us most than any textbook
could about patience, teamwork and where our food really comes from.
